---
title: Getting started
permalink: /getting-started/
---

Install Starlyt as a Git theme, then write ordinary Markdown in your own Jigyll site. The theme supplies the presentation; your site owns its configuration and content.

## Install a consumer

Install Git and Jigyll 1.13.0 or later first. You do not need Node.js, Astro, a Jigyll plugin, or a Sass compiler to use the shipped theme.

From a local checkout named `starlyt`, create a new sibling site:

```sh
jigyll new ../my-docs --theme "$PWD"
```

Run this command from the **Starlyt repository root**, not from an existing consumer. The target must be new. `$PWD` is the local Git source; Jigyll clones its committed contents, not uncommitted edits. A Git URL can be used instead when installing from a hosted repository.

For this project's own documentation, use the repository README's installed-consumer instructions. There is no need to recreate these guide pages yourself.

## Configure your site

Edit `../my-docs/_config.yml`. For a checkout named `starlyt`, a minimal configuration is:

```yaml
title: My documentation
theme: starlyt
url: ""
baseurl: ""
navigation:
  - label: Overview
    link: /
  - label: Installation
    link: /installation/
defaults:
  - scope:
      path: ""
    values:
      layout: default
```

Keep the `theme` value generated by the installer if the source repository has a different name. Jigyll does **not** merge the theme's `_config.yml` or `_data` into your site. Titles, navigation, and layout defaults must be supplied by the consumer.

The [navigation guide](../navigation/) explains nested groups. The [deployment guide](../deployment/) explains `url`, `baseurl`, and portable links.

## Write pages

Replace your consumer's `index.md` with an overview:

```markdown
---
title: Overview
permalink: /
---

Welcome to the documentation.

## Next steps

Read the [installation guide](./installation/).
```

Then create `installation.md` in the consumer:

```markdown
---
title: Installation
permalink: /installation/
---

Install the theme, configure navigation, and build your site.

## Continue reading

Return to the [overview](../).
```

The layout renders the front-matter title as the page H1. Start article sections at H2 instead of repeating that title as another H1. The `permalink` is the public route, independent of the Markdown filename.

## Build and preview

From the Starlyt repository root, build and serve your sibling consumer:

```sh
jigyll build --source ../my-docs
jigyll serve --source ../my-docs --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4322
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:4322/>. The site output is `../my-docs/_site/`; the installed theme is under the consumer's `_theme/` directory. Stop the server with Control-C.

## Override deliberately

A consumer can supply its own layouts, includes, or assets with the same names to override the installed theme. Ordinary documentation should not need those overrides. In particular, this documentation site supplies none: its real layout, styles, and browser enhancements come from the installed theme.

Read [Theme internals](../internals/) before changing shared presentation. Do not turn an example that needs only Markdown into a consumer-specific theme fork.
